column1: # `key` is the row's stable name and never changes; `stage` is what the README
# and the emitted script call it and may carry manifest fields. `since` is the
# first cohort the row applies to, `until` the last (`-` = still current).
# `replaces` names the row a later row supersedes, so a `blocks` edge pointing
# at a retired row follows forward instead of dangling. `cost_sol` is priced
# from the previous cohort's own ledger; `-` moves no lamports. `blocks` names,
# by key, what cannot start until this row is green -- and the emitted scripts
# REFUSE to start until every row that blocks them has left its GREEN marker.
# `shape` is how the generator runs the row: `once` (each invocation once),
# `per-role` (the whole list once per role in the manifest's `roles`),
# `attempts` (the `*` invocations plan-then-sign, a fresh output per attempt),
# `wait:capture` / `wait:settle` (a bounded wait on the market's own schedule,
# a guard that EXITS, then `attempts`), `journal` (the `*` invocations rerun,
# one durable action per pass, until the file each names exists), `commit`
# (a source commit, nothing to run), `-` (the row carries no args yet).
# `args` is the row's invocations, ` ;; ` between them, each starting with its
# driver: `bootstrap` (the job's own successor binary, keyed endpoint),
# it when its --output already exists, `*` marks the attempt/journal act, and
# `*[FILE:field,field]` names what says it is done. `@roles{ ... }` and
# manifest; `{market.x}` against each market the row applies to; `{role}`,
# against the previous cohort's manifest; `{pubkey:keys/x.json}` to the key's
# address at run time; `{execute}` to --execute only under --execute; `{mode}`
# to the word; `{attempt}` to the attempt number; `{stage:key}` to that row's
# output directory for the same market. `$HERE`, `$OUT`, `$CLI`, `$ARGn` and
# the helpers `sha`, `elfsha`, `programdata`, `slot` are the emitted script's.
# A literal typed here instead is a fact with two authors.
# Tabs separate the fields. `check-steps.py --cohort N` gates this file, and
# `--prove-frozen` proves it still reproduces the two tables cohort-14 and
# cohort-15 ran from, kept under frozen/.
